notes: A rate paid is read on chain over a past window. Past rates do not promise future rates.
read_me: The three rates are what the product paid over the last 7, 30 and 90 days, as yearly rates in percent.
A rate is null when it is not known. It is never zero.
read_on is the day of the reading and block the block it was read at. read_on can be older than the data day when that day's reading failed.
A fact shows its answer and its sources once a person has checked it against them. Until then it reads being checked, with no answer and no link.

fact_words.who: who can put money in: anyone with a wallet, or a KYC, allowlist or country limit
fact_words.freeze: whether anyone can freeze or block a holder, and who
fact_words.exit: how a holder gets out, and any wait, cooldown or queue
fact_words.fee: the cut taken from the yield

check_states.confirmed: a person has checked the fact against its sources, so its answer and sources are shown
check_states.being_checked: a person has not checked it yet, so no answer and no source is shown

facts.what: who can put money in: anyone with a wallet, or a KYC, allowlist or country limit
facts.text_as_published: Any wallet holding stETH can wrap it into wstETH. No allowlist is described.

facts.what: whether anyone can freeze or block a holder, and who
facts.text_as_published: No freeze of one holder is described. An emergency committee can pause withdrawals and some core contracts once, for a limited time. The Lido DAO governs all admin roles.

facts.what: how a holder gets out, and any wait, cooldown or queue
facts.text_as_published: A withdrawal queue, normally 1 to 5 days, and slower in stressed markets.

facts.what: the cut taken from the yield
facts.text_as_published: 10% of staking rewards, split between node operators and the Lido DAO.

facts.what: who can put money in: anyone with a wallet, or a KYC, allowlist or country limit
facts.text_as_published: Anyone, with no per-user limit, while the deposit pool has room.

facts.what: whether anyone can freeze or block a holder, and who
facts.text_as_published: No freeze of a holder in the rETH token. A security council chosen by DAO vote can turn off new deposits at once.

facts.what: how a holder gets out, and any wait, cooldown or queue
facts.text_as_published: Swap rETH back to ETH with the protocol when its deposit pool holds enough ETH; otherwise through a swap route outside the protocol.

facts.what: the cut taken from the yield
facts.text_as_published: 14% of rewards goes to node operators (5% base, 9% to operators who stake RPL). The DAO can change it.
